scenes.heading: Zero and negative indices
scenes.sub: What does 2 to the minus 3 mean?
scenes.say: You can't multiply two by itself minus three times. So what does two to the power of negative three mean? Let's find out, and it isn't negative!
scenes.caption: You can't multiply 2 by itself −3 times. So what does 2⁻³ mean? Let's find out, and it isn't negative!

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Each step down a staircase halves your number
scenes.breaks: A staircase has whole steps only, but later you will meet fraction indices too.
scenes.say: Imagine a staircase where every step down divides your number by two. Two cubed is eight. Step down: four, then two, then one at step zero. Keep going below ground: a half, a quarter, an eighth. A negative step doesn't make a negative number. It just means you kept dividing.
scenes.caption: Every step down divides by 2. 2³ = 8. Step down: 4, then 2, then 1 at step 0. Keep going: ½, ¼, ⅛. A negative step doesn't make a negative number. It just means you kept dividing.

scenes.heading: The two new rules
parts: = 1, for any a that is not 0
one over a to the n
scenes.say: Two rules. Anything except zero, to the power zero, is one. And a to the negative n is one over a to the n: the reciprocal. So two to the negative three is one over eight. Think flip, not minus.
scenes.caption: Anything except 0, to the power 0, is 1. And a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ: the reciprocal. So 2⁻³ = 1/8. Think flip, not minus.

scenes.heading: Which part moves?

left.title: 5x⁻²
points: Only x² moves under the line

right.title: (5x)⁻²
points: The bracket moves and is squared

scenes.say: Be careful which part the index belongs to. In five x to the negative two, only the x moves, giving five over x squared. In five x in brackets, to the negative two, the whole bracket moves and is squared: one over twenty-five x squared.
scenes.caption: In 5x⁻², only the x moves: 5/x². In (5x)⁻², the whole bracket moves and is squared: 1/(25x²).

scenes.heading: Evaluate
scenes.question: Evaluate 7⁰ + 3⁻².
scenes.say: Evaluate seven to the zero plus three to the negative two. Seven to the zero is one. Three to the negative two is one over three squared, which is one ninth. Add them: one and one ninth.
scenes.caption: Evaluate 7⁰ + 3⁻². 7⁰ = 1. 3⁻² = 1/3² = 1/9. Add them: 1 1/9.

scenes.heading: Positive indices only
scenes.question: Simplify (3a⁻²)³ × a⁹.
scenes.say: Simplify three a to the negative two, all cubed, times a to the nine. Bracket first: three cubed is twenty-seven, and negative two times three is negative six. Then multiply by a to the nine: negative six plus nine is three. Answer: twenty-seven a cubed.
scenes.caption: Simplify (3a⁻²)³ × a⁹. Bracket first: 3³ = 27 and −2 × 3 = −6. Then times a⁹: −6 + 9 = 3. Answer: 27a³.

points: Only the part with the index moves
All the index laws still work
scenes.say: Recap. Anything except zero, to the power zero, is one. A negative index means flip, not minus. A fraction with a negative index flips over. Only the part with the index moves. And all the index laws still work. Now try the practice questions!
